_note: Danh mục món chuẩn. aliases dùng cho khớp OCR (đã bỏ dấu, chữ thường). Trường `nhin`: dấu hiệu NHÌN THẤY của món, chỉ dùng trong lời nhắc nhận diện món từ ảnh (nhan-mon.js) cho các món dễ nhầm — không hiện ra giao diện.

dishes.desc: Thick chewy noodles, pork slices, greens and crisp croutons — barely any broth. The noodles are made only with water from one ancient well in town.

story.en: The noodles are made with water drawn from one old well in town and lye from Cham Island wood ash — which is why the dish never travelled. Pork, greens, crisp squares, and barely a spoon of broth. The plate carries the marks of a trading port: noodles that look Japanese, roast pork done the Chinese way.
story.vi: Sợi mì làm bằng nước một cái giếng cổ trong phố và tro củi Cù Lao Chàm — nên món này không đi đâu được. Thịt xíu, rau sống, mấy miếng bánh giòn, và gần như không có nước dùng. Trên một cái tô có dấu vết của một thương cảng: sợi mì trông như của người Nhật, thịt xíu làm theo lối người Hoa.
story.src: Giếng Bá Lễ và tro Cù Lao Chàm trong cách làm sợi cao lầu Hội An.

dishes.nhin: thick chewy yellow-brown noodles with almost no broth, slices of char siu pork, fresh greens, square crispy fried noodle croutons.

dishes.desc: Turmeric-yellow noodles in a shallow pool of rich broth, with shrimp, pork, peanuts and a sheet of grilled rice paper you crumble on top.

story.en: A Quang Nam dish, named after the province and not after a city — which is why you find it from Hoi An to Da Nang and rarely further. Turmeric-yellow noodles under just enough broth to wet them, peanuts, and a sesame rice cracker to break over the top.
story.vi: Món của xứ Quảng, mang tên một vùng đất chứ không phải một thành phố — nên gặp nó suốt từ Hội An ra Đà Nẵng, và hiếm khi xa hơn. Sợi mì vàng nghệ, nước lèo chỉ đủ xâm xấp, đậu phộng, và cái bánh tráng mè bẻ vụn lên trên.
story.src: Mì Quảng, món đặc trưng của tỉnh Quảng Nam và Đà Nẵng.

dishes.nhin: wide yellow or white flat noodles with only a little turmeric-tinted broth at the bottom, prawns, pork, quail egg, crushed peanuts and a large sesame rice cracker on top.

dishes.desc: Rice cooked in chicken stock and turmeric, topped with shredded poached chicken, herbs and pickled onion.
Crackly baguette with pâté, cold cuts or grilled meat, pickled carrot and daikon, coriander and chilli.

story.en: The baguette is French. Everything inside it is not: pate, cold cuts, pickled carrot and daikon, coriander, chilli, a spoon of sauce. What the colonial kitchen left behind was refilled with something else entirely.
story.vi: Cái bánh là của người Pháp. Toàn bộ phần bên trong thì không: pa tê, chả, đồ chua, rau mùi, ớt, một thìa nước sốt. Thứ bếp thuộc địa để lại được nhồi vào bằng một thứ hoàn toàn khác.
story.src: Bánh mì Việt Nam, vỏ bánh theo lối baguette Pháp với nhân Việt.

dishes.desc: Crisp fried wonton squares topped with a warm shrimp, pork and tomato salsa. A Hội An specialty, not the soup version.
Translucent rice-flour dumplings shaped like roses, filled with shrimp, topped with fried shallot.
dishes.say: Cho tôi bánh bao bánh vạc
dishes.ph: chaw toy bahn bow bahn vahk

story.en: Called white rose in English, for the shape. Translucent rice dumplings with shrimp or pork inside and fried shallot on top. In Hoi An one family has made them for generations and supplies much of the town, so the version on your plate probably came from the same kitchen as everyone else's.
story.vi: Tiếng Anh gọi là hoa hồng trắng, vì cái dáng của nó. Vỏ bột gạo trong, nhân tôm hoặc thịt, rắc hành phi. Ở Hội An có một nhà làm món này qua nhiều đời và cung cấp cho phần lớn quán trong phố — nên đĩa trước mặt bạn nhiều khả năng ra từ cùng một cái bếp với đĩa của mọi người.
story.src: Bánh bao bánh vạc Hội An, nghề gia truyền của một gia đình trong phố cổ.

dishes.desc: Clear beef broth simmered for hours with charred ginger and star anise, flat rice noodles, spring onion. In Hà Nội it comes plain — no basil plate.
dishes.nhin: FLAT white rice noodles IN clear light-brown beef broth, thin slices of beef (pink/rare or brown), spring onion; no crab, no tomato, no chilli oil slick.

dishes.desc: Charcoal-grilled pork patties and belly floating in a bowl of sweet-sour fish sauce, eaten with cold rice noodles and a mountain of herbs.

story.en: Pork patties and belly grilled over charcoal, dropped straight into a bowl of sweet-sour fish sauce with pickled kohlrabi, eaten with cold rice noodles and a plate of herbs. A lunch dish — the smoke drifting across the pavement at midday is how you find it.
story.vi: Chả viên và thịt ba chỉ nướng than, thả thẳng vào bát nước mắm chua ngọt có su hào ngâm, ăn với bún nguội và một đĩa rau sống. Món của buổi trưa — cứ theo làn khói tạt ngang vỉa hè lúc giữa trưa là thấy.
story.src: Bún chả Hà Nội, món ăn trưa truyền thống.

dishes.nhin: noodles are NOT in the bowl: plain white vermicelli on a separate plate; a smaller bowl of thin amber-orange dipping sauce holds charred grilled pork patties and pork belly, often with floating slices of pickled green papaya/carrot, garlic and chilli; big plate of lettuce and herbs. No crab, no tofu, no tomato wedges.

dishes.desc: Turmeric-marinated fish finished at your table in a pan with an armful of dill and spring onion. Eaten with rice vermicelli, peanuts and shrimp paste.

story.en: Fish marinated in turmeric and galangal, then grilled at your table over a small brazier with dill and spring onion piled on top. One Hanoi family made it famous enough that the street took the dish's name.
story.vi: Cá ướp nghệ và riềng, nướng ngay trên bàn trong chảo nhỏ, phủ đầy thì là và hành lá. Một nhà ở Hà Nội làm món này nổi tới mức cả con phố mang tên món ăn.
story.src: Chả cá, phố Chả Cá trong khu phố cổ Hà Nội mang tên món ăn.

dishes.nhin: yellow turmeric fish pieces sizzling in a pan with lots of dill and spring onion, eaten with vermicelli, peanuts and shrimp paste.

dishes.en: Noodles with tofu and shrimp paste
dishes.desc: A tray of rice noodle sheets, fried tofu, boiled pork and herbs. The dipping sauce is fermented shrimp paste — pungent, purple, and the whole point.
dishes.nhin: a flat tray or bamboo leaf with blocks of fried golden tofu, vermicelli cakes, boiled pork slices, herbs and a small bowl of purple shrimp paste.

dishes.desc: Whipped egg yolk and condensed milk poured over strong coffee. Invented in Hà Nội when milk was scarce. Drink it warm, like a dessert.

story.en: Invented in Hanoi in the 1940s, when fresh milk was hard to come by. Egg yolk whipped with condensed milk until it holds like a custard, poured over black coffee. A shortage turned into a house speciality, and then into the thing the city is known for.
story.vi: Ra đời ở Hà Nội những năm 1940, lúc sữa tươi khó kiếm. Lòng đỏ trứng đánh với sữa đặc tới khi đặc như kem, rót lên cà phê đen. Một cái thiếu thành món tủ của một quán, rồi thành thứ người ta nhớ về thành phố.
story.src: Cà phê trứng Hà Nội, ra đời trong thời kỳ khan hiếm sữa tươi.

dishes.desc: Broken rice grains with a grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, a steamed egg-meat loaf and scallion oil. Saigon's breakfast and its midnight snack.

story.en: Broken rice: the grains that cracked during milling and could not be sold whole. It was what farm workers ate because it was cheap. Now it is the standard Saigon plate — grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, steamed egg cake, pickles.
story.vi: Cơm tấm là hạt gạo gãy trong lúc xay, không bán nguyên hạt được. Trước là cơm của người làm ruộng vì nó rẻ. Giờ là đĩa cơm chuẩn của Sài Gòn — sườn nướng, bì, chả trứng, đồ chua.
story.src: Cơm tấm, nguồn gốc từ gạo tấm là phần hạt gãy khi xay xát.

dishes.nhin: broken rice on a plate with a grilled pork chop, often a shredded pork skin, a steamed egg-meatloaf slice and a fried egg, with pickles and a cup of fish sauce.

dishes.desc: Clear pork broth, chewy tapioca or egg noodles, prawns, pork and quail eggs. Order it 'khô' and the broth comes on the side.

story.en: Came south with Teochew and Khmer cooks and never settled into one recipe. Clear pork broth, chewy noodles, and a dozen versions with a place name attached — Nam Vang, My Tho — plus the dry one where the broth arrives in its own bowl.
story.vi: Theo người Tiều và người Khmer vào Nam, rồi không bao giờ đứng lại ở một công thức. Nước dùng heo trong, sợi dai, và cả chục phiên bản kèm một địa danh — Nam Vang, Mỹ Tho — cộng thêm bản khô, nước để riêng một chén.
story.src: Hủ tiếu, món của cộng đồng người Hoa Triều Châu và Khmer ở Nam Bộ.

dishes.nhin: clear pork broth with translucent chewy noodles, prawns, sliced pork, minced pork, sometimes quail eggs and liver; garlic chives.

dishes.desc: Cold rice noodles under grilled pork, crushed peanuts, pickles and herbs, drowned in sweet fish sauce.
dishes.nhin: a bowl WITHOUT broth: cold vermicelli topped with grilled pork slices, crushed peanuts, fried shallots, pickled carrot/daikon, herbs; fish sauce poured on top or in a small cup; sometimes a cut spring roll.

dishes.desc: Cubes of rice flour cake fried crisp with egg and spring onion, served with green papaya and a soy-vinegar dip. Street food after dark.
Rice paper rolled around prawn, pork, noodles and herbs. Not fried. Dipped in peanut-hoisin sauce.
Crisp fried rolls of minced pork, wood-ear mushroom and glass noodles. Called nem rán in the north, chả giò in the south.
A turmeric rice-flour crêpe stuffed with prawn, pork and bean sprouts. Tear it, wrap it in lettuce and herbs, dip it.
dishes.nhin: large thin crispy yellow crepe folded in half with prawns, pork and bean sprouts inside, served with lettuce and herbs for wrapping.

dishes.desc: Round noodles in a lemongrass and chilli beef broth, sharpened with fermented shrimp paste. Considerably hotter than phở.

story.en: Hue was the imperial capital for more than a century, and the court kitchen left its seasoning behind: lemongrass, chilli oil, shrimp paste. What was cooked for a palace is now sold from a pavement stall before seven in the morning.
story.vi: Huế là kinh đô hơn một thế kỷ, và bếp cung đình để lại cách nêm: sả, ớt màu, ruốc. Thứ từng nấu cho cung điện giờ bán ở gánh vỉa hè trước bảy giờ sáng.
story.src: Bún bò Huế, gia vị đặc trưng sả và ruốc của vùng kinh đô cũ.

dishes.nhin: thick ROUND noodles IN red chilli-oil broth with lemongrass; beef shank slices, a pork knuckle, dark cubes of congealed blood, crab-and-pork balls.

dishes.desc: A whole family of sweet soups — beans, jelly, fruit, coconut milk, over ice. Point at what looks good; every stall makes a different set.
Robusta dripped over condensed milk, poured on ice. Strong enough to reset your afternoon.
dishes.say: Cho tôi cà phê sữa đá
dishes.ph: chaw toy ka feh sua dah

dishes.desc: Light draught beer brewed and delivered daily, poured on street corners. Cheap by design — anything above 15,000₫ a glass is a tourist price.

story.en: Brewed without preservatives, delivered by the keg in the morning, and drunk the same day because it cannot be kept. That is why it costs what it costs, and why it only exists close to a brewery. The plastic stools on the pavement are part of the arrangement, not decoration.
story.vi: Nấu không chất bảo quản, sáng giao từng keg, và uống hết trong ngày vì không để được. Đó là lý do nó rẻ như thế, và lý do nó chỉ có ở gần chỗ nấu. Mấy cái ghế nhựa trên vỉa hè là một phần của cách bán, không phải để trang trí.
story.src: Bia hơi Hà Nội, bia tươi không tiệt trùng nên phải tiêu thụ trong ngày.

dishes.desc: Bottled lager. Larue and Saigon are local and cheap; imported brands cost two to three times more.
A whole young coconut with a straw. Almost always sold at a fixed local price — the classic item to be overcharged on.
Cane pressed to order with a squeeze of calamansi, poured over ice.
Weak iced tea. At most local places it is free or costs a token amount. Being charged more than 5,000₫ is unusual.
Steamed glutinous rice with toppings — mung bean, fried shallot, shredded chicken or pork floss. Breakfast wrapped in a banana leaf.
Paper-thin steamed rice sheets rolled around minced pork and mushroom, showered with fried shallot, dipped in warm fish sauce.

story.en: Rice batter poured onto cloth stretched over a pot of boiling water, steamed into a sheet thinner than paper, lifted off with a bamboo stick and filled while still hot. It has to be made in front of you, which is why it is a morning dish.
story.vi: Bột gạo tráng lên tấm vải căng trên nồi nước sôi, hấp thành lá mỏng hơn tờ giấy, lấy ra bằng cái que tre rồi cuốn nhân lúc còn nóng. Phải làm ngay trước mặt người ăn, nên nó là món của buổi sáng.
story.src: Bánh cuốn, kỹ thuật tráng bánh trên vải căng miệng nồi.

dishes.desc: A simmering pot at your table with plates of raw meat, seafood, noodles and greens to cook yourself. Priced per pot plus per plate — check both.
A sealed cold towel placed on your table. It is not free. If you open it you will be charged, usually 3,000–10,000₫ each.
Boiled pork belly with a rim of fat, rolled at the table in rice paper with a fistful of herbs and green banana, then dipped in fermented anchovy sauce. Ordered as a set for two or more.
dishes.say: Cho tôi bánh tráng cuốn thịt heo
dishes.ph: chaw toy bahn chahng koo-on tit heh-oh

dishes.desc: Clear broth simmered with pumpkin and bamboo shoot, topped with slices of fried and steamed fish cake. The chilli-garlic paste comes on the side, not in the bowl.
dishes.nhin: noodles IN clear pale broth with orange pumpkin chunks and bamboo shoot, topped with slices of golden fried fish cake and white steamed fish cake.

dishes.desc: The turmeric noodles of Quảng Nam served with braised frog legs instead of shrimp and pork — chewier, and cooked with a lot more chilli and lemongrass.
Small river snails stir-fried with lemongrass, chilli and coconut milk. You suck the meat straight out of the shell — that is where the name comes from — and a plate goes with beer, not rice.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một đĩa ốc hút
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot dee-a ock hoot

dishes.desc: Raw herring cured in citrus and rolled in roasted rice powder, wrapped in leaves with a thick fish sauce. From the fishing village at the north edge of the city. It is genuinely raw fish — skip it if that is a problem.
dishes.say: Cho tôi gỏi cá Nam Ô
dishes.ph: chaw toy goy kah nahm oh

story.en: Nam O is a fishing village at the north edge of Da Nang, better known for its fish sauce than for anything cooked. Raw anchovy, roasted rice powder, herbs, and a dipping sauce built on the village's own mam. It exists where the boats land, and nowhere else.
story.vi: Nam Ô là làng chài ở phía bắc Đà Nẵng, nổi tiếng vì nước mắm hơn là vì món nấu. Cá cơm sống, thính gạo rang, rau rừng, chấm bằng chính mắm của làng. Món này có ở chỗ thuyền cập bờ, và không có ở chỗ khác.
story.src: Gỏi cá Nam Ô, làng chài Nam Ô, quận Liên Chiểu, Đà Nẵng.

dishes.desc: Rice paper folded over dried beef floss, quail egg and spring onion oil, grilled crisp over coals and cut into wedges. Street snack, eaten standing up.
Boiled young jackfruit shredded and tossed with pork skin, peanuts, herbs and shallot oil, scooped onto sesame rice crackers.

story.en: Young jackfruit boiled until soft, shredded, then tossed with herbs, peanuts and fried shallot. Served with a sesame rice cracker you break up and use as a spoon.
story.vi: Mít non luộc mềm, xé sợi, trộn với rau thơm, đậu phộng và hành phi. Ăn kèm bánh tráng mè bẻ ra làm thìa xúc.
story.src: Mít trộn Đà Nẵng.

dishes.desc: Dense steamed beef sausage shot through with cracked pepper, sliced into rounds. The city's souvenir food — sold by weight, so check the price per kilo before they cut.
dishes.say: Cho tôi hai lạng chả bò
dishes.ph: chaw toy hai lahng chah baw

dishes.desc: Shredded pig ear and pork skin cured with galangal, garlic and roasted rice, packed in straw bundles and left to sour for a couple of days.

story.en: Pork ear and skin shredded fine, mixed with galangal, garlic, chilli and roasted rice powder, then bound in guava leaves and straw and left to ferment for a couple of days. A way of keeping meat that turned into a thing people buy to take home.
story.vi: Tai và bì heo thái chỉ, trộn riềng, tỏi, ớt và thính gạo, gói lá ổi bó rơm, để lên men vài ngày. Một cách giữ thịt lâu, rồi thành thứ người ta mua về làm quà.
story.src: Tré, món lên men của vùng Đà Nẵng — Bình Định — Huế.

dishes.desc: Agar jelly, mung bean paste and tapioca-coated water chestnut in coconut milk over crushed ice. Cold, cheap and the standard afternoon stop in the heat.
dishes.say: Cho tôi chè xoa xoa hạt lựu
dishes.ph: chaw toy cheh swah swah hat loo

dishes.desc: Blended ripe avocado poured over coconut ice cream with roasted coconut shavings. Sweet, thick, and nothing like avocado anywhere else.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một ly kem bơ
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot lee kem buh

dishes.desc: A finger-thin baguette filled with peppery pâté and chilli. One is a mouthful — people order three or four.
dishes.say: Cho tôi ba cái bánh mì que
dishes.ph: chaw toy bah kai bahn mee kwe

dishes.desc: Thumb-sized steamed rice cakes served in their own little dishes, each dabbed with dried shrimp floss, pork crackling and spring onion oil. Ordered by the tray.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một phần bánh bèo
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot fun bahn beh-oh

story.en: Rice batter steamed in saucers barely wider than a coin, each one topped with dried shrimp and crisp pork fat. Many small dishes rather than one large one is a habit of the court table, and Hue kept it after the court was gone.
story.vi: Bột gạo hấp trong những cái chén nhỉnh hơn đồng xu, mỗi chén rắc tôm chấy và tóp mỡ. Nhiều món nhỏ thay vì một món lớn là nếp của mâm cung đình, và Huế giữ lại nếp ấy sau khi triều đình không còn.
story.src: Bánh bèo Huế, nếp ăn nhiều món nhỏ của ẩm thực cung đình.

dishes.desc: Thin rice batter with shrimp and pork spread flat inside a banana leaf and steamed, eaten straight out of the wrapper with sweet fish sauce.
Translucent chewy tapioca parcels wrapped around a whole shrimp and a sliver of pork belly, steamed in leaf or served bare with chilli fish sauce.

story.en: Tapioca dough wrapped around one shrimp and a sliver of pork, steamed until the wrapper turns clear so you can see what is inside. Sold in banana-leaf parcels, a few bites each.
story.vi: Bột lọc bọc một con tôm với một miếng thịt, hấp tới khi vỏ trong suốt nhìn thấy nhân bên trong. Gói lá chuối, mỗi cái vài miếng là hết.
story.src: Bánh bột lọc Huế.

dishes.desc: Room-temperature rice with baby clams, crackling, peanuts, herbs and roasted chilli, with the clam broth in a bowl on the side. Fiercely hot by default — say “ít cay” if that is not what you want.
dishes.say: Cho tôi cơm hến, ít cay
dishes.ph: chaw toy gum hen, it kai

story.en: Con Hen is a sandbank in the Perfume River. The clams are tiny, raked from the riverbed, and the dish puts them over cold rice with a dozen small toppings and a bowl of the cooking water. It began as a way to make a meal from what the river gave and what the kitchen had left over.
story.vi: Cồn Hến là một bãi bồi giữa sông Hương. Con hến bé xíu, cào lên từ đáy sông, ăn với cơm nguội cùng cả chục thứ rau và một bát nước luộc hến. Món này bắt đầu từ chỗ làm một bữa ăn bằng thứ sông cho và thứ trong bếp còn lại.
story.src: Cơm hến gắn với cồn Hến trên sông Hương, thành phố Huế.

dishes.desc: Fresh rice sheets rolled around charcoal-grilled pork and a bundle of herbs, dipped in a thick sesame-peanut sauce.
dishes.say: Cho tôi bánh ướt thịt nướng
dishes.ph: chaw toy bahn oo-ut tit nuong

dishes.desc: Seasoned minced pork moulded onto lemongrass stalks and grilled, then wrapped in rice paper with herbs and dunked in a thick liver-and-peanut sauce.
Short chewy tapioca-rice noodles in a peppery broth with flaked snakehead fish. Breakfast food, gone by mid-morning.
dishes.say: Cho tôi bánh canh cá lóc
dishes.ph: chaw toy bahn kanh kah lock
dishes.nhin: very thick chewy round tapioca noodles in a slightly thick broth with chunks of snakehead fish, spring onion, fried shallots.

dishes.desc: Robusta dripped over lightly salted whipped cream. The salt takes the edge off the bitterness instead of adding sweetness. Started in Huế, now everywhere.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một ly cà phê muối
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot lee kah-feh moo-oy

story.en: Salted cream whipped over black coffee. Unlike almost everything else on this list it is recent — a Hue invention from the 2010s, young enough that the shop where it started is still open.
story.vi: Kem muối đánh nổi trên cà phê đen. Khác gần như mọi món khác trong danh sách này, nó mới — người Huế nghĩ ra vào những năm 2010, mới tới mức cái quán khởi đầu vẫn còn mở.
story.src: Cà phê muối, xuất phát từ Huế trong thập niên 2010.

dishes.desc: A grilled rice cracker pressed onto a soft steamed rice sheet. You smack it with your palm to shatter it, then tear off pieces and dip them in anchovy sauce.

story.en: Smashed cake, and the name is literal: a crisp grilled rice paper is laid over a soft steamed one, and you hit it with your palm to shatter the top layer before dipping the pieces in fermented anchovy sauce.
story.vi: Bánh đập, và cái tên là nghĩa đen: một lá bánh tráng nướng giòn đặt lên một lá bánh ướt, rồi đập tay cho lớp trên vỡ ra, bẻ từng miếng chấm mắm nêm.
story.src: Bánh đập, món của vùng Quảng Nam — Hội An.

dishes.desc: Baby clams from the river sandbank at Cẩm Nam, tossed with herbs, peanuts, chilli and shallot oil, scooped up on sesame crackers.
Sweetcorn paste rolled thin in rice paper and deep-fried until it shatters, eaten with herbs and a dipping sauce. Usually served alongside bánh đập.

story.en: Corn fritters rolled in rice paper with herbs and dipped in peanut sauce. Same Cam Nam corn as the sweet soup, fried instead of simmered.
story.vi: Bắp chiên cuốn bánh tráng với rau sống, chấm nước tương đậu phộng. Vẫn là bắp Cẩm Nam của nồi chè, chỉ khác là đem chiên.
story.src: Ram bắp Hội An, cùng nguồn bắp Cẩm Nam với chè bắp.

dishes.desc: Young corn grown on the river sandbank cooked into a loose, barely sweet pudding under a spoon of salted coconut cream.

story.en: The corn comes from Cam Nam, the sandy island just across the bridge from the old town. Sweet corn simmered with sugar and coconut milk. The dish is here because the corn is here.
story.vi: Bắp trồng ở Cẩm Nam, cái cồn cát ngay bên kia cầu từ phố cổ. Bắp nấu với đường và nước cốt dừa. Món này có ở đây vì cây bắp ở đây.
story.src: Chè bắp Hội An, bắp trồng trên cồn Cẩm Nam bên sông Thu Bồn.

dishes.desc: Warm, faintly bitter black sesame porridge sold from a shoulder pole. A Chinese remedy dessert that came with the merchants and stayed.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một chén xí mà
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot chen see mah

dishes.desc: Black glutinous rice cake scented with ramie leaf, filled with mung bean and coconut and steamed in a banana-leaf pyramid.
dishes.say: Cho tôi bánh ít lá gai
dishes.ph: chaw toy bahn it lah guy

dishes.desc: The same flat rice noodles as phở bò in a lighter chicken broth, with poached chicken, shredded lime leaf and spring onion.
dishes.nhin: FLAT rice noodles IN clear golden chicken broth with shredded or sliced chicken, lime leaf strips, spring onion.

dishes.desc: Cold rice noodles with quick-seared beef, bean sprouts, herbs, peanuts and fried shallots, with a sweet-sour dressing poured over at the table. No broth, despite the name.
dishes.say: Cho tôi bún bò Nam Bộ
dishes.ph: chaw toy boon baw nahm baw
dishes.nhin: a bowl WITHOUT broth: vermicelli with stir-fried beef, bean sprouts, crushed peanuts, fried shallots, herbs, a little sauce at the bottom.

dishes.desc: Whole prawns in a sweet-potato batter deep-fried into a crisp raft, torn up and eaten with herbs and dipping sauce. The West Lake version is the famous one.
Uncut sheets of fresh phở noodle wrapped around seared beef and herbs, dipped rather than boiled. Invented in the Ngũ Xã lanes when a shop ran out of broth.
A warm, soft pyramid of rice flour around minced pork and wood ear mushroom, unwrapped from its banana leaf and eaten with a spoon.
Shredded green papaya with dried beef, peanuts and herbs under a sweet-sour vinegar dressing, cut to size with scissors in front of you.
A dark, pungent broth built on fermented fish, loaded with squid, prawn, roast pork and aubergine. The smell is the point; the taste is deeper than it smells.
dishes.nhin: noodles IN a murky dark-brown fermented fish broth; squid, prawns, roast pork belly with crackling, purple aubergine chunks.

dishes.desc: Coin-sized turmeric rice pancakes fried crisp in a dimpled pan, each with a prawn on top, wrapped in mustard leaf with herbs before dipping.
dishes.nhin: small round bite-size golden crispy cakes cooked in a mould, each topped with a prawn, served in a group with herbs.

dishes.desc: Beef and carrot stewed soft in a lemongrass-and-annatto broth, eaten with bread or noodles. Breakfast as often as dinner.
dishes.say: Cho tôi bò kho bánh mì
dishes.ph: chaw toy baw kaw bahn mee
dishes.nhin: reddish-orange beef stew with carrot chunks and lemongrass, served with a baguette or noodles.

dishes.desc: A dark, faintly sweet herbal infusion sold cold from roadside urns. Cools you down without the sugar hit of a soft drink.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một ly nước sâm
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot lee nook sahm

dishes.desc: Tomato broth with a raft of freshwater crab and egg, fried tofu, and a spoon of shrimp paste stirred in at the table.
dishes.nhin: noodles sit IN a big bowl of red-orange tomato broth; fluffy brown crab-paste clumps float on top, tomato wedges, fried tofu cubes, sometimes blood cubes or snails. No grilled meat patties.

dishes.desc: Thin rice porridge with sliced pork offal and blood sausage, finished with herbs and a lot of black pepper. Cheap, filling, and not a beginner dish.
Minced beef rolled in wild betel leaves and grilled over coals until the leaf goes dark and fragrant. Wrapped in rice paper with herbs before eating.
Rice paper grilled over coals with egg, spring onion, dried shrimp and chilli sauce spread across it, then folded or cut into wedges.

Live seafood picked from the tank and charged by the kilo. Ask for the price per kilo AND the weight of the exact piece before it goes to the kitchen, and ask them to weigh it in front of you — this is where a bill goes wrong faster than anywhere else in Vietnam.
dishes.say: Bao nhiêu một ký? Cân trước giúp tôi nhé
dishes.ph: bow nyew mot kee? kun chuok zup toy nyeh

dishes.desc: Whole squid grilled over coals and cut into rings, served with a salt-pepper-lime dip. Often priced by weight at seafood places — check before you point.
A small, dense crème caramel served over crushed ice, sometimes with a spoon of coffee poured on top.
Coffee blended with frozen coconut cream into a thick slush. Sweeter and colder than cà phê sữa đá, and closer to a dessert.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một ly cà phê dừa
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot lee kah-feh zoo-a

dishes.desc: Iced milk tea with tapioca pearls or jelly. Sold from chains and from carts; the cart version costs about half.
dishes.say: Cho tôi một ly trà sữa
dishes.ph: chaw toy mot lee chah sooa

dishes.desc: Fresh fruit blended with ice and condensed milk. Say “không sữa” for no condensed milk and “ít đường” for less sugar.
dishes.say: Cho tôi sinh tố, ít đường
dishes.ph: chaw toy sing taw, it duong

dishes.desc: Pressed fruit juice, usually orange, watermelon or passion fruit. Ask for it without added sugar syrup if you want the fruit on its own.
dishes.say: Cho tôi nước ép, không đường
dishes.ph: chaw toy nook ep, khong duong
